claim_one_line: THE JORGENSEN NUMBER: THE THEOREM IS REAL, THE RECORD ALREADY HAD THE NUMBER, AND TWO READINGS DIE. Verifying a forwarded seat report. CONFIRMED: J(m004) = 1.000000000000000 exactly, computed independently by minimising |tr^2 A - 4| + |tr[A,B] - 2| over word pairs on SnapPy's geometric holonomy, attained at the pair (ab, ba) where tr A = -2 (first term 4e-64) and |tr[A,B] - 2| = 1 with tr[A,B] - 2 a primitive cube root of unity; stable at depths 2, 3, 4. Callahan (2009) Cor 2.4 cited, not re-proved. The corpus-absence claims hold ('waist size' 0, 'discreteness bound' 0, every Jorgensen hit being Andersen-Jorgensen, a different person). THE FINDING THE REPORT MISSED, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN ITS CLAIM: at a pair with a PARABOLIC first element tr A = +-2 kills the first term exactly, so J = |tr[A,B] - 2| = |kappa - 2| -- and B309/B518/B1010 bank verbatim 'kappa - 2 = omega^2 with |kappa - 2| = 1, THE UNIT OBSTRUCTION, the founding sentence as an equation'. THE RECORD HAS CARRIED THE JORGENSEN NUMBER AS A HEADLINE LAW FOR HUNDREDS OF ARCS UNDER ANOTHER NAME, without knowing it saturates a 1976 discreteness bound; 'the corpus has never seen this' is half right -- it has never seen the THEOREM and has banked the VALUE, the E54 absent-under-the-other-name shape one level out, between record and literature. B1344's E72 is load-bearing: it is the MERIDIAN kappa that saturates (|omega^2| = 1) while the FIBRE kappa = -2 gives 4, so an unflagged collision would have hidden or falsified the identification. REFUTED (1): '|z| = 1 is the arithmetic shadow of amphichirality' -- if it held, every amphichiral manifold would have J = 1, contradicting the uniqueness theorem cited two paragraphs earlier; computed, the amphichiral knots 6_3, 8_3, 8_9, 8_12, 8_17, 8_18 give 1.4656, 2.3311, 2.7805, 3.2506, 2.0444, 2.4142, chiral 5_2 at 1.3247 sits BELOW amphichiral 6_3, and the report's OWN slack table has amphichiral m136 at 2 sqrt2 and m003 at 4. Its supporting sample (5_2, 6_1, 7_4, 7_7) was ALL CHIRAL so the check could not fail -- the E67 shape. This kills the report's sections 3-4 ('extremality forces symmetry, so the walls are what extremality costs'). REFUTED (2): 'the index vanishes because I = t_0 - r_1 truncates something identically zero by chi(M) = 0' -- B1335 settles it, since on m010 (also one-cusped, also chi = 0) all four identities hold, the sector is in domain D, and I = +-1; and the same fact kills 'no Euler characteristic because it has no slack', since chi(M) = chi(dM)/2 = 0 for EVERY compact 3-manifold with torus boundary at every slack, t12833 far off the bound included. The report's CONCLUSION that filling buys the sign and not the index is correct and already banked (B286 + B1332-B1334); only its mechanism is wrong. SLACK TABLE: 9 of 11 reproduce exactly (m000 1, m004 1, m009 sqrt2, m136 2sqrt2, m003 4, m206 4, v2873 3sqrt3, s958 7, m202 7); t12835 computed 7 against 4, where this bench's length-<=3 search is only an upper bound so the report is probably right; t12833 computed 9 against 13, where the direction is decisive -- J is an infimum and a pair achieving 9 is exhibited, so 13 cannot be it. m000 at J = 1 is NOT a counterexample to uniqueness: m000 is the GIESEKING manifold, NON-orientable, and m004 is exactly its orientable double cover (volume ratio 2.000000), so the report's own table contains the case demonstrating why 'orientable' is in Callahan's statement. WHAT STANDS: the first link really does change type -- J = 1 plus uniqueness is a VARIATIONAL characterisation where every previous selection story was descriptive and measured generic (B762 97.2%, B727, B993 ~1 in 3) -- and the report's own fence travels with it: THIS SELECTS THE MANIFOLD, NOT E6, and everything downstream stays exactly as subject to B727 as before. GATED OBSERVATION, recorded not claimed: the pair attaining the bound is (ab, ba), the image of the Thue-Morse substitution and B497's stratum-3 citizen; whether that is structure or an artefact of short-word search order is UNTESTED. No physics reading licensed, no claim promoted.
